title: Earned media
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What would a journalist want from you?
A student said: marketing is driving sales, and public relations is creating a positive reputation for a person or company through the media.
Another said that a press release cost about fifteen hundred and would be sponsored content, and they had nothing to say.
Jose said that you build earned media, and you have to think how a journalist thinks and what they want.
He suggested: volunteer to write an article for a magazine, offer a case study, write to podcasts in your field, and run a survey with a publication. You have to sell it.
A student suggested combining two ideas: collaborate with local real-estate people and a city magazine on an article about whether branding increases property value.
Jose said he thought that was a great idea, and that you could write to a major firm to publish an article asking whether their business has potential online.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the publications your clients read.
Write the story a journalist would want.
Write a case study you could offer.
Write a survey you could run.
Write the first letter you will send.

check.q: What did a student say public relations is?
choices: Creating a positive reputation through the media

check.q: What did Jose say to think about?
What did Jose say you have to do with the idea?

recap: Earn media. Think like a journalist. Offer a story.
